learning_outcomes.text: Students learn the development process of mathematics in early civilizations.
Students learn mathematics and the methods used in ancient Anatolian civilizations.
The student learns about Turkish-Islamic scientists and mathematicians in the Middle Ages.
Acquires the ability to compare current and past teaching methods and curricula.
Students understand the importance and value of the history of mathematics.

syllabus_topics: Mathematics and Methods in Ancient Anatolian Civilizations
The Founder of Algebra: Al-Khwarizmi and his methods
Islamic Civilization Period: Ebü’l Vefa, Abdülhamid Ibn Türk, Sabit Bin Kurra
Islamic Civilization Period: Abu Ja'far al-Khazini, Ibn al-Haytham, Nasir al-Din al-Tusi, Omar Khayyam
Trigonometry in the Islamic Civilization Period: Al-Battani, Abu al-Wafa, Al-Biruni, Ibn-i Sina
Scientific Developments in Central Asia: Ulugh Beg, Qadi Zada al-Rumi
Introduction of Islamic Science to the West and the Paths of Islamic Civilization to the West
Ottoman Madrasah Curriculum According to Autobiographies and Diplomas of Ottoman Scholars
Mathematics in Ottoman Madrasahs: Gelenbevi Ismail Efendi, Matrakçı Nasuh, Ali Kuşçu, Taqi al-Din al-Rashid
Developments in Mathematics in the Late Ottoman Period: Tevfik Pasha, Gelenbevi İsmail Efendi, Salih Zeki Bey
Student Assignment Presentations, Evaluations and Comments
